guard: a step that resumes a durable pause attaches to the spec already recorded for it — the deadline AND the holder — instead of re-minting from whatever clock and identity it happens to be running under
why: A MINT IS IDEMPOTENT ONLY IF THE WHOLE SPEC IS IDENTICAL, and two halves of the spec are not
identical to themselves across a resume. The deadline, because `now() + duration` is a
different deadline a second later. And the HOLDER, because a resumed run does not necessarily
arrive under the principal that minted its pause: the CLI mints a fresh holder per invocation,
and a cross-host adoption is a different principal by definition. Either way the resumed step
presented a different intent under the same token and the plane refused it, which is exactly
what a one-mint token is supposed to do. The defect was upstream of that refusal: the step
should never have re-minted at all.
Both directions were reproduced live before their repairs. The deadline half on the clock a
real host has: an eight second `sleep` armed, the step performed again 1.2 seconds later under
the id recorded before it ran, and `already exists with a DIFFERENT spec`. The holder half
through the real binary: one `cotal run resume` of a checkpoint-parked run re-minted the pause
under its own fresh holder, the plane refused (`a token is minted once`), and the interpreter
journalled the refusal as the step's own failure — a stranded run, `failed (L4000)`, after a
single resume.
THE SUITES DID NOT CATCH EITHER because every early cell resumed under the same frozen clock
and the same holder, so the mint agreed by coincidence and the cells called it attaching. The
blocks that grade these now let real time pass between the attempts, and mesh-checkpoint's
takeover block resumes under a DIFFERENT holder.
AND A PAUSE CAN COME BACK OVERDUE. A mint refuses a deadline in the past, correctly, so an
unarmed pause whose deadline elapsed while the host was away cannot be repaired by minting it
again. The reconciler re-emits its schedule at the status's current generation instead, and
the fire that follows is what ends it. The reconciler is also the attach path for a successor
holder, which is why the two share one exit in arm().

mutations.name: the recorded deadline is ignored, so an own-holder resume re-mints from its own clock
mutations.completionMarker: • 2 — the same step after a crash
mutations.expectRed: the resumed attempt was not refused
mutations.cell: the resumed attempt was not refused: it attaches to the recorded pause rather than re-minting
mutations.note: The shipped defect's deadline half, one expression wide inside the own-holder retry branch. Measured 2026-09-02 before this entry was written: cells print through block 1, block 2 reds on this cell with `already exists with a DIFFERENT spec`. It reddens as a refusal rather than as a hang, which is the one merciful thing about it: the run stops on a named conflict instead of waiting forever. What it does not do is resume.

mutations.name: the overdue guard is dropped, so a past deadline is re-minted and refused
mutations.completionMarker: • 3 — a resume that arrives after its own deadline, never armed
mutations.expectRed: the overdue resume is not refused
mutations.cell: the overdue resume is not refused: a past deadline is reconciled, not re-minted
mutations.note: A mint requires a future deadline, so this turns the overdue resume into a `failed-precondition`. The distinction the guard draws is not tidiness: a pause that is due is not being armed, it is being collected, and those are different operations on the plane. Measured 2026-09-02: block 3 reds on this cell first, with the plane's own future-deadline refusal in the extra.

mutations.name: the overdue pause is recognised and then nothing is done about it
mutations.completionMarker: • 3 — a resume that arrives after its own deadline, never armed
mutations.expectRed: the overdue sleep did not end within 20000ms
mutations.cell: the overdue sleep did not end within 20000ms
mutations.note: The silent direction, and the reason the cell it reddens carries its own deadline: nothing throws, nothing is wrong, and the schedule nobody armed is never asked for again. The pause is due, unarmed and permanent, which is the same shape as the fire that had no caller. A guard against a hang asserted by a bare `await` is not weak, it is ungradeable -- the tool scores a timeout inconclusive by its own correct rule that a hang is not a red.

mutations.name: PAIRED: the recorded deadline is ignored, graded on the `wait` timeout rather than on `sleep`
mutations.expectRed: the re-performed wait was not refused
mutations.cell: the re-performed wait was not refused: it attaches to the timeout already minted for it
mutations.note: THE SAME BRANCH SERVES THREE EFFECTS, and a repair claimed for one of them is a claim about all three until something grades the others. `wait` arms its timeout through the same helper, and its clock was always the real one, so what it was missing was the gap: a block that performs a pending wait again after real time has passed. That block exists and this entry is what proves it is grading the deadline rather than watching a wait time out the way it always did.
